original_verdict.reason: Step 3.1 says the additive group has exponent exactly p, including the trivial group. The trivial group has exponent 1, so [F1] only supports exponent dividing p in that case.
Step 2.1 relies on the triangle inequality, but L4 cites lem-of-abs-value, whose supplied interface does not include it. Add the missing dependency or prove the inequality.

The first remark is false: a nowhere-dense subset of R cannot contain a nondegenerate interval, since that would give it nonempty interior. So a closed nowhere-dense set cannot “fill an interval” as claimed.

The title and precise statement promise an injection using rationals in (lim_{x→c⁻}f(x), lim_{x→c⁺}f(x)) for every monotone f. For a nonincreasing function with an interior jump, the left limit is greater than the right, so this interval is empty; the proof only establishes the c
Step 3.1 misstates Froda’s theorem as permitting every at-most-countable discontinuity set. Its interface gives only the upper bound; the realization theorem [L2] supplies the converse.

The proof does not handle dimension 0. Step 1.2 applies Euclidean nullity and cube-cover budgets, but the supplied Euclidean definition is for dimensions m≥1; [L1] instead requires chart images to be empty. Split off the 0-manifold case to establish the union claim.

Step 1.1 applies L1 to the prescribed A- and B-atlas charts, but its interface guarantees nullity transfer only in some coordinate neighborhoods, not those fixed chart coordinates. The transfer to ψ(E∩W_j), needed for the core implication, is unproved.

Step 1.1 attributes a specific Cantor-set construction and the formula F(x,y)=g(x)+g(y) to [L1], but its supplied interface establishes only existence of some F with critical values containing [0,2]. Those construction details are unlicensed.

Step 5.1 relies on every rational being m/n (m∈Z, n≥1), but no cited interface states that representation: the supplied integer-to-rational item gives only an embedding, and the rational-to-real item gives an ordered-field embedding. L3 and step 5.1 use an unlicensed dependency.

The vocabulary claim is false: first kind includes both removable and jump discontinuities, and one-sided points can also be removable. Rudin’s two kinds do not name the same three cases, so the title’s claimed equivalence is inaccurate.
